title: Definition Directory and Navigation Hub are both specified at the .0.0 position, an unresolved collision
content:
Two Type Specifications in this chunk claim the same position. A.1.2.2.2.21: "Definition Directory Documents must always be located at the .0.0 position of their Target Document." A.1.2.2.2.25: "Navigation Hub Documents must be located at the .0.0 position of an Immutable or Primary Document."

Both use "must," both are Supporting Documents, and the Target Documents overlap — Definition Directories serve "Target Documents with many complex subdocuments," which is precisely the population that most needs a Navigation Hub. So the two rules collide on exactly the documents where both types are most likely to be required.

This matters more than a numbering nit because the whole categorization scheme rests on identifiers being unique and positionally meaningful (A.1.2.1.1, A.1.2.2.1): a document's address determines its category, its mutability, and its relationship to other documents. Two types mandating one address is a defect in the addressing layer itself, not in a single document's content.

There is a partial mitigation in the text: A.1.2.2.2.21 says Definition Directories "only need to be present in Atlas Documents that require definitions for unique terms in their Subdocuments," so the conflict is conditional rather than universal. But conditional is not resolved — nothing states which type yields, or where the loser goes.

This is squarely the class of contradiction A.1.1.2.1 empowers the Core Facilitator to fix by Atlas Interpretation: different Atlas documents conflicting "leading to confusion or inconsistency in their application." It is recorded here as an open item rather than an inference about intent.
description: A.1.2.2.2.21 places Definition Directories at .0.0 of their Target Document while A.1.2.2.2.25 places Navigation Hubs at .0.0 of Immutable or Primary Documents
